# A difference of two limbs rounded up, on values of the program

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `sub_up_entry` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$a - b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$r = \mathrm{RU}(a - b).$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \mathrm{RU}(a - b)$: the smallest number of the format not below $a - b$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `sub_up_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v), against `sub_up_entry_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions sub_up_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition sub_up_entry_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let r := sub_up_entry emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = RU emin prec (a - b).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $b$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $r$ is the smallest number of `T` not below $a - b$, or $+\infty$ when $a - b > \Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $r = a - b$, as `T` computes it.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `sub_up_entry_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeEntry.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeEntry.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions sub_up_entry_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `sub_up_entry_correct` and `sub_up_entry_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** sub_up_1 on its guarded operands (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/sub_up_entry.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/sub_up_entry.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`sub_up_1`](sub_up_1.md).

```
# RU(a - b) for the public building block kairn::sub_up (milestone2.md, "Values that enter from
# the program"): both operands pass through guard, then sub_up_1. The statement is sub_up_1's, in
# both models; not claimed: the sign of a zero result, which the guard can change.

ga = guard(a)
gb = guard(b)
r  = sub_up_1(ga, gb)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
